overreach: non-signaling test comes earlier and deeper at the RF/PHY characterization level
signaling test comes later when the RFIC is integrated enough to behave like a real wireless device/system
Silicon bring-up / bench debug → Non-signaling tester
RF parametric validation → Non-signaling tester → TX power, EVM, ACLR, SEM, phase noise...
Production test → Usually non-signaling for speed/cost
For semiconductor RFIC validation, the non-signaling setup is usually the main workhorse
The DUT is not necessarily running a full protocol stack
CMP180 ... aligns more with RF/waveform-centric non-signaling or production-style validation use cases
Signaling tester fits once the RFIC is part of a larger platform — RFIC + baseband/modem + protocol stack + firmware
review.reason: The cited passages support that the CMX500 is a signaling tester for end-to-end signaling, RF conformance, protocol validation, and real-world signaling-mode RF TX/RX measurements, and that the CMP180 can verify waveform bandwidth in loopback for R&D/production. They do not substantiate the detailed RFIC validation workflow, the role and timing of non-signaling testing, production-test claims, or most listed RF measurements.
